fixture reattest: the real answer of reattest for a held capture: unacknowledged by default (every authority refused, no attestation, the attempts appended late), acknowledged when an authority grants and the archive replays the same bytes

fixture storageNotConfigured: acquire on an instance with no evidence store is refused 503 EVIDENCE_STORAGE_NOT_CONFIGURED, its check and translation the installation's

fixture captureArm: a real capture over a scripted network files what the route serves, answers a refusal the source gives, records each call and each reader registration, and refuses an unknown or a second reader as capture does

fixture reattest: the real answer of reattest for a held capture: unacknowledged by default (every authority refused, no attestation, the attempts appended late), acknowledged when an authority grants and the archive replays the same bytes

fixture captureAccount: the real answer of recordCaptureAccount by the capturing member is the first account, signed over the statement with the member's key, and captureAccountsOf reads it back; a member who did not capture it is refused

R113 (abandoned): an abandoned upload is aborted and holds nothing: by the member's abort, by the expiry stated (24 hours after its begin, swept at the next begin), and when its owner comes back after it

tests: R113 (G127f): a file of three parts over the injected cap is begun, its parts put, and completed into ONE whole under its whole digest, registered with ONE job row in the filing transaction, and answered as `uploadCapture` answers a one-request upload
R113 (control): a file under the cap still goes in one request, unchanged: no multipart upload is made and the answer is `uploadCapture`'s

R113 (the digest of all the bytes): the whole's digest is hashed in order across the parts, never a part's: a first part's digest declared as the whole is refused at the completion, the upload aborted and nothing held; two equal parts are two parts
R113 (a part's digest is checked as it arrives): a part that does not hash to its digest stores nothing; a part put twice is idempotent and stored once; other bytes under a held index are refused

R113 (order): a part past the next is refused with the next one named and nothing stored; a completion with a part missing or out of order is refused and writes nothing, and the upload stays open to be finished

R113 and R111 (the ceilings): the declared size is judged before any part: over `CAPTURE_MAX` is refused 413 with size and bound and no upload is begun; at the ceiling it is begun; a part of another size is refused with nothing kept, its body read and discarded (G176)
R113 (the byte ledger): the ledger holds at most one part at a time across a whole parted upload, and is empty after every path, a refused part included; a part is held once, not twice

R113 (the member's own): only the member who began an upload may put, complete or abort it (another reads as an unknown upload); the begin is refused as an upload is, writing nothing: no member session, no statement, a name or type that is not a string

R113 (abandoned): an abandoned upload is aborted and holds nothing: by the member's abort, by the expiry stated (24 hours after its begin, swept at the next begin), and when its owner comes back after it

R113 (G173, an instance taken out of memory between parts): the next part in order is accepted by an instance that has none of the hashing in memory, and the completion's digest is the declared one; a wrong part and a wrong whole are still refused
R114 (G180): a parted upload interrupted after its second part and resumed from the row's snapshot files the digest of the whole; the snapshot is the one record-grammar's stream takes up

R113 (G173, UPLOAD_LOST only when the digest cannot be told): an open upload whose row keeps no digest of its parts (begun before it was kept) or one that does not describe the parts held is aborted and answered UPLOAD_LOST, nothing held; a begin of the same file again by the same member abandons the first
R113 (one part at a time): a second put of an index whose bytes are still arriving is refused and disturbs nothing

R113 and R109 (the filing): a refusing registrar rolls the whole filing back, naming the job, with the object held and the upload retryable; `within` is called once inside the transaction and its refusal rolls back likewise; a retry files the same object
R113 and R109 (no registrar): with none the answer says so, as an upload in one request does, and the file is otherwise filed

R113 and R110 (an archive): a ZIP sent in parts registers an `unpack` row beside its `reading` row, as an uploaded one does; text sent in parts is profiled from its declared type as one in a request is (R92, R107)

R113 (the same file again): bytes the evidence store already holds are begun as held with no part to send, and the completion files them as a second sighting; a different member's second upload leaves one job row

R78 (DEC-97 (3)): a registered batch examination answers each row eligible, or not with the class it fails first and its reason; one that fails or answers neither reads null, undetermined; registered once

R82 (K1129): an unknown sweep answers 0, as does a sweep that is no string; heldCount writes nothing and never throws: a store that cannot be read answers null, never 0

R77 R83 (DEC-141 (1)): each held row answers captured_for for the viewer: every question it may see with title and asker, and the one withheld sentence, with no id, title, asker or count, when a question it may not see is among them; captured for nothing answers [] and null

R79 R83 R84 (DEC-141 (1), (2)): a set-aside reads each document's questions once, before writing, and records every question waiting on it, seen by the viewer or not, with that set-aside; the one reason applies to each in a batch; the answer names captured_for and the waiting questions as the viewer is shown them

R108 (control and the second member): a one-part upload is unchanged, and two members uploading the same bytes share the whole's digest and no part's

R109 (G126, K4835 (2)): an upload registers its `reading` row through the registrar inside its own transaction, one row keyed by the whole sha, and arms the alarm after the commit; a second upload of the same bytes leaves one row

R109 (a kill between the put and the transaction): the parts are stored first and the filing is one transaction: an upload cut before it leaves no row and no receipt, and its retry leaves exactly one row; a refusing registrar rolls the upload back with no receipt and no actor and is answered as a stated refusal
R109 (control): the same upload with no registrar says so in its answer and is otherwise filed as R86 states

R109 (keep): past MULTIPART_KEEP_MAX the keep handed to the plane is the `keep` row, registered in the same transaction with the parts, and the answer says keep_pending; the store is not asked by the upload

R111 (G124b, G124g; K4838 (6)): a body one byte past the platform's request ceiling is refused 413 naming its size and the ceiling, the stream cancelled and no receipt, actor or row written; a body at the ceiling is accepted; the figure is the runtime-limits entry, quoted

R111 (the table's ceiling): CAPTURE_MAX is the archive row of READ_BOUNDS, and when it is the smaller figure it is the one named; an injected lower figure of either kind is honoured and a higher one never raises the real ceiling
R111 (G124b): a 24 MiB text upload is counted by the byte ledger: its peak is the file and at most two parts beyond it, and nothing is held once it is answered

R111 (the sentences): a refusal carries the key of its sentence and the figure, never a literal of this module's own: the request ceiling's key is this module's stand-in, the capture ceiling's is the table row's

R112 (control and the waiting answer): a render that succeeds is charged as before, an unreported render stays charged, and a `waiting` answer carries its running slots and cap and no account of the day

R109 (G152, K4958; control-plane R125 (a), R132): a PDF stated over the whole-read ceiling of its kind registers no `reading` row and says so; the same bytes under it, and a kind with a higher row, still register theirs
R109 (G152, K4958): a single-part upload hands the bytes it holds to the profile: the evidence store is asked for no whole object, for a PDF or a text, and the profile is what a read-back would give

R110 (G126f, X3; DOCS A1, A12): an uploaded ZIP of three text members registers an `unpack` row for its whole sha with its `reading` row, and is then opened as a fetched archive is: each member filed, read separately, and the archive's entries are not `waiting`; uploaded twice it opens once
R110 (control): an upload that is not an archive registers no `unpack` row, and a refused registrar for the archive rolls the upload back
